templates.label: Character Basics
templates.description: Core character questions for planning or revision.

items.title: Want
items.body: What does the character consciously want?

items.title: Need
items.body: What do they actually need to learn, accept, or become?

items.title: Lie / Flaw
items.body: What false belief or behavior keeps them from the need?

items.title: Ghost / Wound
items.body: What past experience helps explain the lie or flaw?

items.title: Stakes
items.body: What do they stand to lose if they do not change?

items.title: Contradiction
items.body: What makes them more complicated than their surface trait?

templates.label: Character Arc
templates.description: A flexible change arc from starting state to ending state.

items.title: Beginning State
items.body: Who are they before the story forces change?

items.title: Want
items.body: What are they actively trying to get?

items.title: Need
items.body: What truth or change do they actually need?

items.title: Lie / Flaw
items.body: What belief or behavior blocks that need?

items.title: Pressure
items.body: How does the story repeatedly test the lie or flaw?

items.title: Realization
items.body: When do they begin to understand what must change?

items.title: Crisis Choice
items.body: What difficult choice proves whether they can change?

items.title: Change
items.body: What new action demonstrates the transformation?

items.title: Ending State
items.body: Who are they now, and what visibly contrasts the beginning?

templates.label: Save the Cat Beats
templates.description: The 15-beat Save the Cat story structure.

items.title: Opening Image
items.body: A snapshot of the story world and protagonist before the transformation.

items.title: Theme Stated
items.body: A hint at the lesson or truth the story will explore.

items.title: Setup
items.body: Establish the protagonist, ordinary pressures, relationships, goals, and flaws.

items.title: Catalyst
items.body: The event that disrupts the existing life and makes the old normal unstable.

items.title: Debate
items.body: The protagonist hesitates, resists, or weighs what entering the story will cost.

items.title: Break into Two
items.body: A decisive move into the unfamiliar world or main story problem.

items.title: B Story
items.body: A secondary relationship or storyline that often carries the theme.

items.title: Fun and Games
items.body: The premise delivers on its central promise while complications grow.

items.title: Midpoint
items.body: A major reversal, false victory, or false defeat that raises the stakes.

items.title: Bad Guys Close In
items.body: External pressure and internal flaws tighten around the protagonist.

items.title: All Is Lost
items.body: The apparent lowest point, when the current approach seems to have failed.

items.title: Dark Night of the Soul
items.body: The protagonist processes the loss and confronts what must change.

items.title: Break into Three
items.body: A new understanding creates a new plan that combines what has been learned.

items.title: Finale
items.body: The protagonist acts on the new understanding and resolves the central conflict.

items.title: Final Image
items.body: A closing snapshot that shows how the world or protagonist has changed.

templates.label: Hero's Journey
templates.description: A 12-stage Hero's Journey based on the commonly used modern story model.

items.title: Ordinary World
items.body: Show the hero's life before the central adventure begins.

items.title: Call to Adventure
items.body: A challenge, opportunity, or threat invites the hero into change.

items.title: Refusal of the Call
items.body: Fear, duty, doubt, or circumstance makes the hero resist.

items.title: Meeting the Mentor
items.body: Guidance, training, tools, or confidence prepares the hero to proceed.

items.title: Crossing the Threshold
items.body: The hero commits and enters the unfamiliar world of the adventure.

items.title: Tests, Allies, Enemies
items.body: The new world reveals its rules through challenges, relationships, and opposition.

items.title: Approach
items.body: The hero prepares for a dangerous confrontation near the heart of the problem.

items.title: Ordeal
items.body: A central crisis forces the hero through a major fear, loss, or confrontation.

items.title: Reward
items.body: Surviving the ordeal brings knowledge, reconciliation, an object, or another gain.

items.title: The Road Back
items.body: Consequences pursue the hero as they turn toward resolution or home.

items.title: Resurrection
items.body: A final test requires the hero to demonstrate the transformation at the highest stakes.

items.title: Return with the Elixir
items.body: The hero returns with something that changes or benefits the ordinary world.

items.title: You
items.body: A character exists in a zone of comfort.

items.title: Need
items.body: They want or need something that disturbs that comfort.

items.title: Go
items.body: They enter an unfamiliar situation.

items.title: Search
items.body: They adapt, struggle, and learn the rules of the new situation.

items.title: Find
items.body: They get what they wanted, or reach the thing they were pursuing.

items.title: Take
items.body: Getting it carries a cost or consequence.

items.title: Return
items.body: They return toward a familiar situation.

items.title: Change
items.body: They are now capable of acting differently because of the journey.

templates.label: Seven Point Story Structure
templates.description: Seven major turning points from hook to resolution.

items.title: Hook
items.body: Establish the protagonist and the starting condition that the ending will transform.

items.title: Plot Turn 1
items.body: Introduce the conflict strongly enough to pull the protagonist into the story.

items.title: Pinch Point 1
items.body: Apply direct pressure from the antagonistic force or central problem.

items.title: Midpoint
items.body: Shift the protagonist from reaction toward more deliberate action.

items.title: Pinch Point 2
items.body: Apply stronger pressure and make failure feel immediate or costly.

items.title: Plot Turn 2
items.body: Provide the final information, realization, or resource needed for the climax.

items.title: Resolution
items.body: Resolve the central conflict and demonstrate the resulting change.

templates.label: Three-Act Structure
templates.description: A practical beat map across setup, confrontation, and resolution.

items.title: Act I — Setup
items.body: Establish the world, protagonist, central tensions, and the life that cannot remain unchanged.

items.title: Inciting Incident
items.body: Introduce the disruption that begins the central story problem.

items.title: First Plot Point
items.body: A commitment or consequence closes the setup and launches the main confrontation.

items.title: Act II — Confrontation
items.body: The protagonist pursues the goal, meets escalating obstacles, and learns through failure.

items.title: Midpoint
items.body: A central reversal changes the stakes, understanding, or direction of the conflict.

items.title: Second Plot Point
items.body: A final major turn prepares the protagonist for the decisive confrontation.

items.title: Act III — Resolution
items.body: The climax resolves the central conflict and the aftermath shows what changed.

templates.label: Freytag's Pyramid
templates.description: A five-part dramatic arc centered on a climax.

items.title: Exposition
items.body: Introduce the dramatic situation, characters, and necessary context.

items.title: Rising Action
items.body: Complications and conflicts build toward the central turning point.

items.title: Climax
items.body: The dramatic conflict reaches its decisive peak.

items.title: Falling Action
items.body: The consequences of the climax unfold and remaining conflicts narrow.

items.title: Resolution
items.body: The dramatic action settles into its final state.

templates.label: Kishōtenketsu
templates.description: A four-part structure built around introduction, development, twist, and integration.

items.title: Ki — Introduction
items.body: Introduce the subject, situation, or pattern.

items.title: Shō — Development
items.body: Develop what was introduced and deepen the audience's understanding of it.

items.title: Ten — Twist
items.body: Introduce an unexpected element, contrast, or shift in perspective.

items.title: Ketsu — Conclusion
items.body: Connect the earlier material and the twist into a satisfying whole.
